nodes.title: Consideration and Bargained-for Exchange
nodes.conceptSummary:
### 1. Pangkal Anomali
Di pergaulan sosial kita biasa menjanjikan hadiah atas dasar rasa terima kasih. Namun ketika seorang majikan berjanji memberikan bonus pensiun atas 30 tahun jasa masa lalu lalu mengingkarinya, hukum menolak menegakkan janji tersebut sebagai kontrak yang sah.

### 2. Prototipe Intuitif
Bayangkan timbangan jungkat-jungkit dua arah. Sebuah kontrak hanya bisa bergerak seimbang jika beban ditaruh serentak di kedua sisi: Anda memberikan nilai X karena pihak lain menyerahkan nilai Y sebagai imbalan tawar-menawar langsung (bargained-for exchange).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    PartyA["Pihak A (Pengorbanan Hukum)"] <-->|Bargained-For Exchange| PartyB["Pihak B (Manfaat Hukum)"]
```

### 3. Invarian & Operasi Inti
Invarian mutlak sistem adalah **Mutualitas Kewajiban (Consideration)**: prestasi yang telah selesai di masa lalu (past consideration) tidak memiliki nilai timbal balik untuk mengikat janji baru.

forwardPass.prompt: "Predict whether an employer's promise to pay a retiring employee an extra bonus 'in gratitude for 30 years of past loyal service' forms an enforceable contract."

options.text: Unenforceable for lack of consideration: past consideration was not bargained-for in exchange for the new promise, unless promissory estoppel or written statutory reliance applies.
options.causalRationale: Correct: Past service cannot serve as fresh bargained-for exchange for a future promise.

options.text: Enforceable because 30 years of loyal service constitutes sufficient moral obligation.
options.causalRationale: Moral Obligation Fallacy: Moral gratitude is not recognized as legal consideration in contract law.

options.text: Enforceable under the doctrine of substantial performance.
options.causalRationale: Doctrine Confusion: Substantial performance applies to breach remedies, not formation consideration.

forwardPass.groundTruth: "Unenforceable for lack of consideration: past consideration was not bargained-for in exchange for the new promise, unless promissory estoppel or written statutory reliance applies."
